items.title: MiniMax：2月公司ARR（年度经常性收入）超过1.5亿美元
items.raw_excerpt: 36氪获悉，3月2日晚，MiniMax 创始人、CEO 闫俊杰在电话会上透露，2026年2月公司 ARR（年度经常性收入）已超过1.5亿美元，面向企业客户和个人开发者的开放平台产品，2026年2月新注册用户数已经达到2025年12月的4倍以上。业绩报显示，MiniMax 2025年实现总收入7903.8万美元，同比增长158.9%。其中，AI 原生产品收入5307.5万美元，同比增长143.4%。

title_i18n.zh: MiniMax：2月公司ARR（年度经常性收入）超过1.5亿美元
title_i18n.en: MiniMax: The company's ARR (Annual Recurring Revenue) exceeded $150 million in February.
title_i18n.es: MiniMax: En febrero, los ingresos recurrentes anuales de la empresa superaron los 150 millones de dólares.

excerpt_i18n.zh: 36氪获悉，3月2日晚，MiniMax 创始人、CEO 闫俊杰在电话会上透露，2026年2月公司 ARR（年度经常性收入）已超过1.5亿美元，面向企业客户和个人开发者的开放平台产品，2026年2月新注册用户数已经达到2025年12月的4倍以上。业绩报显示，MiniMax 2025年实现总收入7903.8万美元，同比增长158.9%。其中，AI 原生产品收入5307.5万美元，同比增长143.4%。
excerpt_i18n.en: 36Kr learned that on the evening of March 2, Yan Junjie, founder and CEO of MiniMax, revealed during a conference call that the company's ARR (Annual Recurring Revenue) had exceeded $150 million by February 2026. For its open platform products targeting enterprise clients and individual developers, new user registrations in February 2026 had grown to over four times the level of December 2025. According to the performance report, MiniMax achieved total revenue of $79.038 million in 2025, a year-on-year increase of 158.9%. Among this, revenue from AI-native products amounted to $53.075 million, up 143.4% year-on-year.
excerpt_i18n.es: 36Kr se ha enterado de que en la noche del 2 de marzo, Yan Junjie, fundador y CEO de MiniMax, reveló en una conferencia telefónica que en febrero de 2026 el ARR (ingresos anuales recurrentes) de la empresa ya superaba los 150 millones de dólares. En cuanto a los productos de plataforma abierta dirigidos a clientes empresariales y desarrolladores individuales, el número de nuevos usuarios registrados en febrero de 2026 alcanzó más de 4 veces el de diciembre de 2025. El informe de resultados muestra que MiniMax obtuvo unos ingresos totales de 79,038 millones de dólares en 2025, un aumento interanual del 158,9%. De estos, los ingresos por productos nativos de IA fueron de 53,075 millones de dólares, con un crecimiento interanual del 143,4%.

items.title: Parallax – Coordinate adversarial AI agents over durable streams
items.raw_excerpt: Parallax is a CLI for orchestrating independent AI agent cohorts (Claude, Codex, etc.) over isolated, append-only logs or streams. Each cohort operates on its own log and does not see the intermediate reasoning of others i.e. disagreement is enforced at the infrastructure layer rather than prompted at runtime. Agents write to sequenced, durable logs and a separate moderator agent subscribes to all streams, monitors progress, issues steering instructions when necessary, and synthesizes outputs at the end. That means, coordination is just done over a log with natural language, which allows us to rewire topology of agents mid-run, fork, merge, spawn breakout rooms or build any research methodology on the fly depending on the question. items.title: We filed 99 patents for deterministic AI governance(Prior Art vs. RLHF)
items.raw_excerpt: For the last few months, we've been working on a fundamental architectural shift in how autonomous agents are governed. The current industry standard relies almost entirely on probabilistic alignment (RLHF, system prompts, constitutional training). It works until it's jailbroken or the context window overflows. A statistical disposition is not a security boundary. We've built an alternative: Deterministic Policy Gates. In our architecture, the LLM is completely stripped of execution power. It can only generate an "intent payload." items.title: Agd – a content-addressed DAG for tracking what AI agents do

When your agent breaks something, you get to grep through a wall of output in some proprietery system. Why can't i easily see what the agent did to produce the PR? why can't i restart a different agent from a state? It works like git (blobs, trees, refs, immutable objects identified by hash), but the object types are specific to LLM interactions: messages with typed content parts, tool definitions, and workspace snapshots that form a causal graph. Why can't i easily see what the agent did to produce the PR? why can't i restart a different agent from a state? I got tired of this. agd is a content-addressed object store and causal DAG for recording agent behavior. It works like git (blobs, trees, refs, immutable objects identified by hash), but the object types are specific to LLM interactions: messages with typed content parts, tool definitions, and workspace snapshots that form a causal graph. The core idea is stolen from git: the data model is the API. You interact with objects directly. Everything is immutable,
excerpt_i18n.zh: 每个代理框架都会提供日志（各有各的风格）。非结构化文本。运气好的话，可能还有些跨度信息。当你的代理搞砸了什么，你就得在某个专有系统里，面对一堵输出墙，用grep去翻找。
excerpt_i18n.es: Cada framework de agentes te proporciona registros (cada uno con su propio estilo de registros). Texto no estructurado. Quizás algunos intervalos si tienes suerte. Cuando tu agente rompe algo, tienes que buscar a través de un muro de salida en algún sistema propietario.

items.title: I built a sub-500ms latency voice agent from scratch
items.raw_excerpt: I built a voice agent from scratch that averages ~400ms end-to-end latency (phone stop → first syllable). That’s with full STT → LLM → TTS in the loop, clean barge-ins, and no precomputed responses. What moved the needle: Voice is a turn-taking problem, not a transcription problem. VAD alone fails; you need semantic end-of-turn detection. The system reduces to one loop: speaking vs listening. The two transitions - cancel instantly on barge-in, respond instantly on end-of-turn - define the experience. STT → LLM → TTS must stream. Sequential pipelines are dead on arrival for natural conversation. TTFT dominates everything. In voice, the first token is the critical path. Groq’s ~80ms TTFT was the single biggest win. Geography matters more than prompts. Colocate everything or you lose before y

items.title: 智械盛宴下的孤岛：AI、资本与知识生态的隐秘危机
items.raw_excerpt: 近年来，人工智能（AI）对就业、产业创新以及知识生态的影响成为社会热议话题。媒体和舆论常强调 AI 可能取代大量岗位，引发焦虑。然而，从实际观察来看，AI 对就业和产品生态的影响远比“全面失业”或“无限增长”复杂，需要理性分析，同时结合后疫情时期的全球经济环境、资本市场压力、企业行为模式以及 LLM（大型语言模型）提供方对产品迭代的控制。

title_i18n.zh: 智械盛宴下的孤岛：AI、资本与知识生态的隐秘危机
title_i18n.en: Isolated in the Feast of Intelligent Machines: The Hidden Crisis of AI, Capital, and the Knowledge Ecosystem.
title_i18n.es: Isla solitaria bajo el festín de la maquinaria inteligente: la crisis oculta de la IA, el capital y el ecosistema del conocimiento.

excerpt_i18n.zh: 近年来，人工智能（AI）对就业、产业创新以及知识生态的影响成为社会热议话题。媒体和舆论常强调 AI 可能取代大量岗位，引发焦虑。然而，从实际观察来看，AI 对就业和产品生态的影响远比“全面失业”或“无限增长”复杂，需要理性分析，同时结合后疫情时期的全球经济环境、资本市场压力、企业行为模式以及 LLM（大型语言模型）提供方对产品迭代的控制。
excerpt_i18n.en: In recent years, the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on employment, industrial innovation, and the knowledge ecosystem has become a widely discussed topic in society. Media and public discourse often emphasize AI's potential to replace numerous jobs, sparking anxiety. However, from a practical perspective, AI's influence on employment and product ecosystems is far more complex than scenarios of "mass unemployment" or "unlimited growth," requiring rational analysis that also considers the global economic environment in the post-pandemic era, capital market pressures, corporate behavior patterns, and the control over product iteration by LLM (large language model) providers.
excerpt_i18n.es: En los últimos años, el impacto de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en el empleo, la innovación industrial y el ecosistema del conocimiento se ha convertido en un tema de amplio debate social. Los medios y la opinión pública suelen destacar que la IA podría reemplazar numerosos puestos de trabajo, generando ansiedad. Sin embargo, desde una observación práctica, el efecto de la IA en el empleo y el ecosistema de productos es mucho más complejo que un "desempleo masivo" o un "crecimiento ilimitado", requiriendo un análisis racional que considere el entorno económico global posterior a la pandemia, las presiones del mercado de capitales, los modelos de comportamiento empresarial y el control que los proveedores de modelos de lenguaje grandes (LLM) ejercen sobre la iteración de productos.

excerpt_i18n.en: Hi HN! My name is Rohan and, together with Paul, I’m the co-founder of OctaPulse ( https://www.tryoctapulse.com/ ). We’re building a robotics layer for seafood production, starting with automated fish inspection. We are currently deployed at our first production site with the largest trout producer in North America. You might be wondering how the heck we got into this with no background in aquaculture or the ocean industry. We are both from coastal communities. I am from Goa, India and Paul is from Malta and Puerto Rico. Seafood is deeply tied to both our cultures and communities. We saw firsthand the damage being done to our oceans and how wild fish stocks are being fished to near extinction. We also learned that fish is the main protein source for almost 55% of the world's population. De
